title: Carbonara
subtitle: Roman pasta with guanciale, egg yolk, and Pecorino Romano
excerpt: One of the four great Roman pastas: spaghetti tossed off the heat with a creamy sauce of egg yolks, Pecorino Romano, Parmesan, and crisped guanciale. No cream, no onion.

recipe.sourceNotes: Carbonara is one of the four great Roman pasta dishes (with cacio e pepe, amatriciana, and gricia). The origin of the dish is debated: some attribute it to Roman cuisine from before the Second World War; others link it to American soldiers who brought bacon and eggs to Rome during the Allied liberation in 1944, which combined with local pasta traditions. The authentic Roman version uses guanciale (cured pig cheek), Pecorino Romano, and a generous quantity of coarsely ground black pepper, with eggs used for richness. Cream is never added in the Roman tradition; the creaminess comes entirely from the emulsion of egg yolk and pasta water created off the heat. The critical technique is temperature control: the eggs must not scramble. The pan is removed from the heat before the sauce is added, and pasta water and vigorous tossing are used to emulsify the sauce into a silky, coating consistency.

recipeTools.notes: A large saucepan for the pasta. A wide frying pan for the guanciale and sauce.

content.text: The sauce is made entirely off the heat. Remove the frying pan from the heat source before adding the pasta and the egg mixture. The residual heat of the pan and the pasta is enough to cook the eggs into a silky sauce if you toss vigorously and add pasta water a tablespoon at a time to control the consistency. If the pan is too hot the eggs will scramble; if too cold the sauce will not emulsify. Work quickly and do not stop tossing until the sauce is smooth and coats every strand.

Whisk the egg yolks, whole egg, Pecorino, and Parmesan together in a bowl. Season with the black pepper. Set aside. Cook the pasta in well-salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve 250 ml of the pasta cooking water.
While the pasta cooks, fry the lardons in the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes until the fat has rendered and they are golden. Remove from the heat.

Add the drained pasta to the pan with the lardons. Toss well. The pan must no longer be on the heat. Add a tablespoon of pasta water and toss again. Pour the egg mixture over the pasta and toss vigorously, adding pasta water a tablespoon at a time until the sauce is silky and coats every strand. Serve immediately.
